extracted.intended_audience: registrants (public companies), corporate accounting and financial reporting teams, auditors, and outside counsel/advisers who interact with the SEC staff
extracted.subtask_description: Best-practice guidance for registrants and their advisers on communicating with the SEC staff, resolving comment letters, requesting waivers (Rule 3-13), and seeking informal interpretive guidance from the Division of Corporation Finance (CF-OCA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt review and timely response to comment letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the comment letter immediately and respond to the SEC staff reviewer (named in the letter) within the time indicated in the comment letter (usually 10 business days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If possible, the registrant should not request an extension, since this may delay resolution of the comment letter. However, in certain circumstances, the registrant should consider requesting an extension to provide a more thorough and complete response that addresses all of the staff’s comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek clarification when comments are not understood
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant does not fully understand any specific comment, it should contact its SEC staff reviewer quickly for clarification so that it can provide an appropriate response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess impact on ability to issue financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the impact the comment letter may have on its ability to issue the financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unresolved comments may affect a registrant’s ability to issue financial statements and an auditor’s ability to issue the current-year audit report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult SEC legal counsel regarding certification impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult with its SEC legal counsel about the impact the comment letter may have on the certifications contained in its Form 10-K or Form 10-Q.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult auditors on audit-report implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult with its auditors to discuss the impact the comment letter may have on their ability to issue the current-year audit report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support responses with authoritative accounting literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Include in the response a discussion of supporting authoritative accounting literature and references to the specific paragraph(s) from the standard(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When calling the staff with an interpretive or procedural question, do not assume that the staff has all the facts. Responding registrants should do the appropriate research, provide sufficient background information, and present an analysis that points to relevant authoritative literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider including requested future disclosures in response letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Because some comments may request disclosure in future filings, the registrant should consider including such disclosure in the response letter to potentially eliminate additional requests from its SEC staff reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: If disclosure is immaterial, explain immateriality
rubrics_metrics.description: If an immaterial disclosure is requested, the registrant should consider explaining why the disclosure is immaterial instead of including the immaterial disclosure in future filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain regular contact and communicate timing constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain contact with its SEC staff reviewer and make the reviewer aware of the registrant’s required timing (on the basis of its current-year filing deadlines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow up if no response within two weeks
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant has not received a follow-up letter or been contacted within two weeks of filing the initial response letter, the registrant should contact its SEC staff reviewer to determine the status of the comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The registrant should promptly address any follow-up questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirm review completion and request completion letter
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant is uncertain about whether its review has been completed without further comments, it should ask the SEC staff reviewer about the status of the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the review is complete, the registrant should ask the reviewer for a completion letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize questions are not conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Just because the staff asks a question does not mean that it has reached a conclusion or that a change is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid agreeing to future disclosures solely to expedite review
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant should not agree to include a disclosure in future filings solely to expedite the completion of a review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate immateriality positions early
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant believes that a comment concerns an immaterial matter, the registrant should communicate that belief to the staff early in the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious analogizing to other registrants' facts
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant should use caution when analogizing to other registrants’ fact patterns since a small difference in facts could make a meaningful difference in the response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide staff sufficient time to evaluate new information
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant should ensure that the SEC staff is provided enough time to appropriately evaluate substantive new information during the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide contact information for company and outside counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the staff with contact information for the responding company and its outside counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly and directly address all issues raised
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly and directly address all issues raised in the comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: When calling staff, present background and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: When calling the staff with an interpretive or procedural question, do not assume that the staff has all the facts; do the appropriate research, provide sufficient background information, and present an analysis that points to relevant authoritative literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider staff review scope beyond filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of the staff’s review encompasses information beyond the review of specific filings to include other information, such as press releases, information on a registrant’s Web site, analyst calls, investor presentations, and other documents such as sustainability reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants should be aware that public communications beyond the filing may be reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask staff preferences and document oral comments
rubrics_metrics.description: If the SEC staff provides oral comments, the registrant should ask the SEC staff reviewer how he or she would like to receive the registrant’s response to the oral comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reviewer requests a response via EDGAR, respond with a written letter. If the reviewer requests an oral response or identifies no preference, the registrant should still consider responding with a letter to formally document the registrant’s understanding of the staff’s comments and the discussions held as well as the registrant’s response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect proactive staff contact on significant events
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC staff may also contact a registrant to discuss publicly reported significant events, such as a cyber breach affecting the registrant, before commencing a review or issuing any written comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of material unresolved comments in Form 10-K (Securities Offering Reform)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Securities Offering Reform, large accelerated filers, accelerated filers, and well-known seasoned issuers must disclose in their Forms 10-K the substance of any material unresolved SEC staff comments that were issued 180 or more days before the end of the current fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a filing obligation and affects certain categories of filers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use CF-OCA for waivers and interpretive assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The CF-OCA performs functions that may result in communications with companies and their advisers, including acting on behalf of the Commission to grant relief under Rule 3-13, answering interpretive request letters and providing informal interpretive advice, and helping identify and explain applicable rules, regulations, forms, and guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider engaging CF-OCA when seeking relief or interpretive guidance on financial statement form and content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be thorough and provide all relevant facts in Rule 3-13 prefiling letters
rubrics_metrics.description: When a registrant prepares a prefiling letter to request a waiver from the CF-OCA, be thorough and provide all relevant facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propose solutions and provide adequate support in waiver requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose solutions and adequate support for the proposals when requesting Rule 3-13 relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain how waiver request is consistent with investor protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Include support related to why the waiver request is consistent with the protection of investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate waiver requests with auditors
rubrics_metrics.description: Show the letter to the registrant’s auditors and have them weigh in before sending it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide full significance-test results for acquisition-related requests
rubrics_metrics.description: For requests related to acquisitions, provide the results of all significance tests, including the inputs used if the calculations are not straightforward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss waiver fact patterns with staff by phone before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC staff has indicated that it is available to discuss potential waiver fact patterns by phone in advance of a registrant’s submission of a written request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pre-submission discussions to clarify expectations and needed support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of Rule 3-13 waiver requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples include omission of one or more years of historical financial statements for a recently acquired business subject to Rule 3-05 and omission of certain financial statements of an equity method investment subject to Rule 3-09.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit Rule 3-13 relief requests via online form
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for relief under Rule 3-13 should be submitted by online form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit prefiling letters to OCA for complex accounting matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants are encouraged to submit a prefiling letter to the OCA on the proposed application of U.S. GAAP to resolve complex accounting issues before filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For best practices related to consulting with the OCA, see the guidance on the SEC’s Web site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal interpretive guidance is nonbinding
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants may reach out to the CF-OCA to seek informal interpretive guidance on a named or unnamed basis by e-mail, phone, or online form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given the nature of the informal discussions, statements made by the staff are intended to be helpful but cannot be relied upon since they are not binding.
